answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the low-cost vendor's quote meets it on its own, so a primary move is required to hit the cost target. c2 confirms that vendor has delivered before with fast onboarding and accurate invoicing, which is the highest-leverage fact to re-verify before committing a single-slot decision. c6 and c4 inform the negotiation wrapper around the switch: sign a multi-year term only if volume pricing is granted, and benchmark the quote against market rates before locking, so we recover margin on price and payment terms without widening the service scope. A 94% utilization line with no buffer means the switch must be staged as a parallel-run with a short overlap window, keeping the incumbent on month-to-month until the new vendor proves out, rather than a hard cutover. Verification budget is spent on c2 because the decision turns on whether the low-cost vendor's reliability in practice still holds; c1's integration-stability point is secondary since the swap is being deliberately staged. One-second-source hedging is deferred to the next review cycle to preserve budget for the primary move this cycle.
